title_orig: Confutatio legis latae Saracenis a maledicto Mahometo (in the print: 'Richardi fratris ord. Praedicatorum, Confutatio legis a Mahumete Saracenis latae, e Graeco Demetrij Cydonij Latinitate donata, Bartholomeo Piceno interprete')
title_es: Refutación de la ley que los sarracenos recibieron de Mahoma (Riccoldo da Monte di Croce)
title_en: Refutation of the Law that the Saracens received from Muhammad (Riccoldo da Monte di Croce)
date: original Latin c. 1300 (not read); the Latin text quoted is a back-translation from Kydones' Greek, printed 1550 (Basel)
language: Latin (16th-century print of a Latin version of a Greek version of the original)
genre: Polemical refutation of the Qur'an (apologetic treatise, chapters with headings such as 'De impudicitia eius & flagitijs')
edition_original: Machumetis Saracenorum principis, eiusque successorum vitae, doctrina, ac ipse Alcoran ... Basileae (Basel): Ioannes Oporinus, 1550 (ed. Theodor Bibliander). Scan: archive.org item case_bp127_l3_1550 (Newberry Library). Quoted page: PDF page 268 of that scan (printed pp. 7-8 of the section).
digital_url: https://archive.org/details/case_bp127_l3_1550  (PDF page 268, read as page image at 300 dpi and checked at 600 dpi)
licence: The Latin text (1550) is public domain. The archive.org item metadata says 'All rights reserved by the Newberry Library. Permission to reproduce in any format must be requested in writing.' That restriction covers the scan, not the 1550 text: quote the words, do not reproduce images.
authenticity_note: Riccoldo's authorship of the Confutatio is accepted in the literature. The Latin printed here is NOT Riccoldo's own Latin: the print says it was translated from Latin into Greek by Demetrius Kydones and then back into Latin by Bartholomaeus Picenus. Wording therefore reflects a Greek intermediary. The 1550 section boundaries were not verified beyond the title page and the chapter heading; attribution rests on the match with the 1606 printing (same Zaynab and Mary stories).
notes: Companion printing: Riccoldo (Ricardi) Confutatio, Venice: apud Aloysium Zannettum, 1606 (archive.org bub_gb_u0DM9SzvBlMC, PDF page 49 read). The 1606 printing contains the Aiefe/Mary passage but the Ali/young-virgin passage was NOT found in it (searched pages 40-130 of the PDF text layer). The English 'Refutation of the Koran' (Londini Ensis, 2010, self-published, in copyright) was consulted only to locate the Mary story and is NOT quoted. Numeric ages: none found in the Latin read.

title_orig: Ricardi ex ordine fratrum, qui apud Latinos, Praedicatores appellantur. Confutatio legis latae Saracenis a maledicto Mahometo, translata ex Romana lingua in Graecam, per Demetrium Cydonium. Deinde per Bartholomaeum Picenum de Monte arduo, rursus e Graeco in Latinum
title_es: Refutación de la ley de los sarracenos (Riccoldo da Monte di Croce)
title_en: Confutation of the law brought to the Saracens (Riccoldo da Monte di Croce)
date: 1606 (print); see riccoldo_confutatio_1550 for the textual history
edition_original: Venice: apud Aloysium Zannettum, 1606. Google Books scan via archive.org item bub_gb_u0DM9SzvBlMC (PDF page 49 read as page image at 400 dpi).
licence: archive.org metadata: Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0 (licenseurl http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/).
authenticity_note: Same textual history as the 1550 print (Kydones' Greek, then Picenus' Latin). Printed page numbers on the scan were not determined.
notes: Printed 'Aiefe, filia Empipecer' (Empipecer read from the page image; probably a corruption for Abubacer / Abu Bakr; not resolved).

title_orig: Machumetis, Saracenorum principis, eiusque successorum vitae, doctrina, ac ipse Alcoran (section 'Qualiter ... recollectum' / on the second collection and dispersal of the Qur'an; the print's contents list calls the dossier 'Codex authenticus doctrinae Machumeticae, ex Arabico versus per Robertum Retenensem & Hermannum Dalmatam')
title_es: Dosier latino cluniacense sobre Mahoma y el Corán
title_en: Latin Cluniac dossier on Muhammad and the Qur'an
date: Latin translation c. 1143 (per the 1543/1550 title page: 'ante annos CCCC'); Arabic original not identified
genre: Translated Muslim account of Muhammad, his life and the Qur'an, with Latin marginalia
edition_original: Basel: Ioannes Oporinus, 1550 (ed. Theodor Bibliander), same volume as riccoldo_confutatio_1550. Quoted page: PDF page 272 (printed pp. 15-16 of the section).
digital_url: https://archive.org/details/case_bp127_l3_1550  (PDF page 272, read as page image at 300 dpi)
licence: As for riccoldo_confutatio_1550: 1550 text public domain; the scan is 'All rights reserved by the Newberry Library'.
authenticity_note: The Latin text is an 1143 translation of an Arabic work (per the title page). Its Arabic source is not identified here; treat the report as a Muslim tradition reported in Latin, not as Christian commentary.
notes: The Latin dossier also contains a section on Muhammad's life and generation ('De generatione Machumet et nutritura eius', text-layer index line 14507ff; PDF page not determined), in which no Aisha passage was found in the text layer.

title_orig: Cribratio Alkorani, Liber secundus (Cribrationum Alcorani libri tres, Domini Nicolai de Cusa Cardinalis)
title_en: Sifting of the Qur'an (Nicholas of Cusa)
genre: Learned polemic/critique of the Qur'an, in three books
edition_original: Printed in Basel: Ioannes Oporinus, 1550 (ed. Theodor Bibliander), same volume as riccoldo_confutatio_1550. Quoted page: PDF page 309 (printed p. 89, left column of the spread), read as page image at 300 dpi.
licence: 1550 text public domain; scan 'All rights reserved by the Newberry Library' (see above).
authenticity_note: Authentic Cusanus text. The 1461 Heidelberg critical edition (in copyright) was not consulted.
notes: No mention of Aisha or of any wife's age was found in Liber secundus or Liber tertius of the 1550 text layer; the passage quoted deals with the Qur'an's permission of many wives. Another line (PDF p. 322, text layer only) states 'cum Mahumet XL. annorum' (Muhammad aged forty when converted from idolatry by the monk Sergius); not an Aisha passage.

title_orig: Historia Hierosolymitana (Jacobus de Vitriaco), opening section on Muhammad
genre: Crusade chronicle with an introductory account of Islam
edition_original: Gesta Dei per Francos, sive orientalium expeditionum et regni Francorum Hierosolymitani historia, Hanau: Typis Wechelianis, apud heredes Ioan. Aubrii, 1611 (ed. Jacques Bongars), vol. 1-2 scan. Read from the djvu text layer only (OCR).
digital_url: https://archive.org/details/GestaDeiPerFrancosSiveOrientaliuT1et2 (djvu text layer; printed page not determined)
licence: archive.org metadata: Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0.
authenticity_note: The 1611 edition attributes the Historia Hierosolymitana to Vitry; the editor's preface says it was reconstructed from a damaged manuscript and an Oliver of Paderborn letter (see the preface pages of the same volume). Attribution of the Muhammad section to Vitry is accepted as the edition's own statement.
notes: OCR only: the quoted sentence was read from the text layer and NOT checked against the page image. Vitry names no wife and gives no age.
